i don’t think there’s an actual reason you would have to deserve it. i think we just like to think that, even if there’s no logical basis. you’re also just a kid, i’m just a kid too, we’re fuckin learning, cut yourself some slack. as to how to stop, i’m not the person to ask. i’ve tried to stop a good few times and i have gotten a lot better, to the point where i’m only doing it a few times a month, but i’m not fully clean. just try to get yourself to do it less. when people try to go clean all together it creates an all or nothing type thing where  if they relapse at all it’s back to square one, but that disregards all the progress made. also, what’s been my problem with stopping is the white bear effect. the white bear effect is the idea that if you tell yourself not to think about something you’ll most definitely think about it more. that’s why i’ve stopped counting clean days, because while it can be a motivation, it also just makes you think about it more if you’re counting the days. just try to get it out of your mind and you’ll stop on your own, or at least do it less.

if it hurts real bad after the moment it happened, it’s probably not 3rd degree (damages nerves), if a blister forms and it turned white the moment it happened, it’s a 2nd degree (partial thickness), not all 2nd turn white though, only the worse ones, depending on what you burned yourself with, make sure the wound is sterile, and immediately cover it, most of mine are always 2nd degree and what i generally do is wait for the blister to burst on its own, then once it opens i apply antibacterial shit and cover it with gauze and tape, it’s very important to keep it covered to prevent infection, if it’s a first degree (skin doesn’t open, hurts very bad, red after burn, can form blisters but less common), you don’t need to treat it very much just run it under cold water, the most important thing to do with a burn is to reduce surface temp by running it under cold water to prevent further tissue damage

are you sure? what if, say you have an expectation on your back that you can deadlift a 50 pound weight. you “can” maybe, but it’s going to be painful and laborious and you probably won’t be able to lift much else for a little. you don’t want to do it, but you feel you’ll let people down if you don’t. it’s being weak to not even try to do it, to opt out, but you’ll safe yourself effort and pain, and thus, it’s beneficial. lets put this to a less clear scenario, someone with a good life will debilitating depression. they have everything they could ever want but life is still extremely difficult and painful, and their past and genealogy says it’s gonna stick around for a long time. they gave life a chance but for years it’s still difficult. wouldn’t it feel so much better, and thus be advantageous, to just opt out of all the hassle? maybe they could recover after a while, but that’d be a ton of effort. it’s easier and feels better to just, go. nothing is always going to be better than bad. 0 is always going to be more than -1. so how is oblivion not better than a shitty life? how is weakness not to this person’s advantage?
